text:
Predicates:
Schedules(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
Customer(y) ::: y is a customer.
InCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemoteFromHome(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James (constant).

Premises:
∀x (Schedules(x, y) → Employee(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (∃y (LunchInCompany(x)) → ∃y (Schedules(x, y))) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x) → RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ RemoteFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ∧ (Manager(James) ∨ ¬InCompanyToday(James)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.

Conclusion:
¬InCompanyToday(James) ::: James has lunch in the company.
